message.content: {"caption":"An informational workflow diagram showing how reports guide alternating model and skill updates in a CoWork example.","description":"A green-and-white, bordered infographic titled “Report-driven co-evolution | CoWork example.” It sets the task as processing a CSV, preserving row order, and submitting checked output; the traces and report excerpts are synthetic, and update axes alternate across rounds. Panel (a), “Execution evidence and failure attribution,” is a three-column table (Stage, Trace / artifact, Diagnostic evidence). S3: row-order check skipped and no test output; the required skill exists, but policy skips it. S4: after restart, trial-results.json is used without opening it; the skill omits retrieval and validation in the new workspace. Beneath the table, the LLM attribution rule says to pool scores and traces across development tasks and exclude infrastructure failures. Panel (b), “LLM Report,” targets S3 if it has the most frequent model-attributed failures, attributes these to a skipped known verification procedure, and requests prioritizing S3 practice while retaining adjacent stages and end-to-end tasks. Panel (c), “Harness Report,” identifies the gap as no artifact check after workspace restart; its Add skill sequence runs left to right: retrieve → open → validate saved output. Its recovery instruction is to try allowed recovery, then stop and report if the artifact remains unavailable. Panel (d), “Model update | harness frozen,” gives the left-to-right training sequence fresh rollouts → verified rubric rewards → GRPO. The gate allows a development-score drop of at most 20% relative to the accepted checkpoint; rejection means restoring that checkpoint. Panel (e), “Skill update | model frozen,” tests the same tasks and model with and without the edit while tools and execution rules stay fixed. Its gate requires self-tests and safety, improvement at the target stage, an overall gain of at least 5 percentage points, and no end-to-end regression; rejection means keeping the current harness. A bottom “Next round” band gives the left-to-right sequence evaluate retained pair → regenerate reports → alternate update axis, followed by the note that accepted skills shape training and updated models reveal the next skill gap. The panels are separated by rules; there are no plotted data, check marks, or crosses.","figure_type":"diagram","chart_values":[]}
